title: Truck driver arrested after he was caught hauling oversized load at night with no permit and suspended CDL, Missouri sheriff says

Login Truck driver arrested after he was caught hauling oversized load at night with no permit and suspended CDL, Missouri sheriff says
 PCSO Published:
 November 20, 2026 By Ashley Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Copy URL A Missouri sheriff arrested a truck driver hauling an oversized load without a permit, warning devices, or a valid commercial driver license (CDL).
 On October 27, 2026, a deputy with the Platte County Sheriff’s Office (PCSO) Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Unit spotted a commercial truck hauling an oversized load on I-29 “during darkness, without warning devices and oversize load banners.”
 The deputy initiated a traffic stop and conducted an inspection.
 PCSO During the inspection, the deputy discovered that the truck driver’s CDL was suspended and that he did not possess an oversized load permit from the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT).
 The width of the oversized load was over 13 feet, police said.
 PCSO Additionally, eight Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulation (FMCSR) violations were discovered during the inspection.
 “The for-hire Louisiana motor carrier and driver were placed out-of-service, and the driver was custodially arrested,” PCSO said.
 During an “inventory” of the truck’s sleeper berth, police located warning devices and an oversized banner.
 PCSO The truck was towed from the scene.
 The Platte County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office requested and received an arrest warrant for the driver.
 PCSO “Two days later, after posting bond upon his arrest warrant,” the same PCSO deputy saw the semi truck hauling the same oversized load on Route 92, this time with warning devices and oversized banners.
 “Having knowledge a MoDOT permit had still not been obtained, the Deputy stopped and inspected the tractor-trailer again. The driver had now obtained a valid CDL but still lacked a MoDOT permit,” the sheriff’s office said.
 During the inspection, 15 FMCSR violations were discovered.
 A court summons was issued, and the driver was assisted with obtaining a permit from MoDOT.
